detailed_description: CSS Clip Path Generator helps you assemble a CSS clip-path declaration with a fast preset-and-text workflow. Choose a preset such as Triangle, Diamond, Star, Circle, or Inset, or type your own circle(), ellipse(), polygon(), or inset() value in the textarea. The preview square updates so you can check the basic shape, and the output area shows the exact clip-path line to copy. Use it for quick layout masks, image crops, and hero-section shapes when you already know the value you want to refine.
usage_steps: Choose one of the built-in presets to start with a common clip-path value.
Edit the clip-path text directly if you need a custom circle(), ellipse(), polygon(), or inset() shape.
Check the preview square to confirm the shape looks close to what you need.
Copy the generated clip-path declaration and paste it into your CSS.
Test the copied declaration in the real responsive layout before publishing it.
usage_examples: Create a triangle or diamond mask for a decorative section divider.
Test a polygon value before adding it to a hero image or card design.
Copy a simple circle or inset clip-path for a prototype without writing the declaration from scratch.
Keep a set of quick CSS shape snippets for layout experiments.

faqs.question: Can I edit the clip-path value manually?
faqs.answer: Yes. The textarea accepts CSS clip-path values such as circle(), ellipse(), polygon(), and inset().

faqs.question: What does the copy button include?
faqs.answer: It copies a CSS declaration in the form clip-path: value; using the current value shown in the tool.

faqs.question: Does the tool export image or SVG files?
faqs.answer: No. It produces a CSS clip-path declaration for you to use in your own stylesheet.

faqs.question: Can I move points on a canvas?
faqs.answer: No. The current tool uses presets plus direct text editing in the textarea, then shows a simple preview.

faqs.question: Does it check browser support?
faqs.answer: No. It creates the CSS declaration only, so test the final value in the browsers and breakpoints you support.
